title: Weather and Interior
premise: Mirabel Amberdale has spent twenty years cataloguing the night at the Halcyon Branch Library, guarding a secret: the fire that killed her father was set by her brother, and her mother's silence bought the family its survival. When the childhood house goes to auction, her brother Theo returns to bid on it, forcing the family's careful arrangement into the open. Mirabel must finally speak the truth she has shelved for two decades, choosing honesty over the fragile peace it will destroy — and in doing so, loses the house but gains her brother, her mother's confession, and at last the courage to say what she has almost said to her colleague Anselm for twenty years. The novel ends not with belonging restored but with belonging rebuilt, on ground that has burned and been honestly cleared.
about_author: Quentin Marchetti is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in a coastal city that never fully slept. 'Weather and Interior' is his second novel, following a well-received debut about lighthouse keepers and their unsent letters.

chapters.title: The Hours That Belong to No One
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A night shift at the Halcyon Branch: shelving, a drunk poet, Anselm's quiet company, and the auction notice for the Amberdale house that she reads three times without breathing. Emotional beat: the practiced calm of a woman who has made avoidance into craft, cracked by a single envelope.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Burned Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with a flashback to the fire when she was nine. She visits the empty house before the auction, standing in the room where her father died, cataloguing what remains like library holdings. Emotional beat: grief that has been misfiled for twenty years, surfacing in the smell of scorched plaster.

chapters.title: Theo Comes Back for the Furniture
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Her brother arrives in town with money he shouldn't have and a plan to buy the house, charming the auctioneer and lying easily. Emotional beat: the seductive comfort of the family fiction, and Theo's awareness — barely admitted — that he is buying back the scene of his crime.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept in the Attic
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Her mother, Vivian, now sharp-tongued in a care home, warns her not to attend the auction. In the attic boxes Mirabel finds her father's letters and a fire marshal's report her mother never surrendered. Emotional beat: the dawning horror that the silence was not grief but arrangement.

chapters.title: Anselm, Who Waits Without Asking
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. He tends the library's failing heating system and Mirabel's unspoken life with equal patience; a near-confession over coffee at 3 a.m. dissolves when she flinches. Emotional beat: love against duty — his duty to respect her silence warring with his wish to be let in.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Theo outbids a developer; Mirabel stands up in the crowded hall and says, publicly, that the house should burn rather than be bought. Emotional beat: rising tension breaking — the first public crack in twenty years of arrangement, and the family's faces turning toward her like weather.

chapters.title: Conflagration, Second Attempt
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. That night he drives to the house intending to burn it himself and end the question forever; Mirabel arrives to stop him, and in the dark kitchen he finally says what happened — the argument, the lamp, the panic. Emotional beat: climax — the truth spoken at last, and it is worse and smaller than she feared.

chapters.title: Vivian's Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She brings the fire marshal's report to her mother, who confesses she knew and paid to keep it quiet, believing she was saving her children. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit — a mother who bought peace with her daughter's trust, and the terrible tenderness of understanding why.

chapters.title: Everything Shelved, Everything Withdrawn
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The house sells to the developer after all; Theo, unburdened, leaves town lighter than he came. Mirabel files the report, quits nothing, changes everything — and at closing time stands in the empty stacks unable to speak again. Emotional beat: the old habit of almost saying it, one last time.

chapters.title: Weather and Interior
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A storm knocks out the power; she and Anselm sit in the dark among the books, and she tells him everything — the fire, the silence, the years. He stays. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging not as a house or a family arrangement, but as a person who hears the whole interior and remains.
